A)  Multi-level analysis:  the relation between self-reported goal attainment and changes in outcomes.

```{r}
rm(list = ls(all = TRUE)) # Clear workspace

library(dplyr)
library(skimr)
library(readxl)
library(tidyr)
library(openxlsx)
library(data.table)
library(readxl) # excel sheet

DataDir<-""
OutDir<-""


# Terugblik data (imputed version)
tb<-fread(
  paste0(DataDir,"2026-04-01_TerugblikIMP_export_260331.csv"),
  sep=";", 
  fill=TRUE)
tb<-as.data.frame(tb)

# noncompleted
tb<-tb[!tb$Studienummer %in% c("B17" ,"B21", "B23_original"),]
table(tb$Studienummer)

# load PDT results
pdt <- read_excel(paste0(OutDir, "2026-04-03_Summary_ITSA_PDT.xlsx"), sheet = "PDT")
#pdt<-pdt %>% select(Studienummer, effect_FSE, effect_Satisfaction, effect_Health)
pdt<-pdt[!pdt$Studienummer=="B17" & !pdt$Studienummer=="B21",]

```

# A -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# create the goal compliance var
```{r}

tb <- tb %>%
  mutate(
    goal_numeric = case_when(
      goal_check_daily_string == "Het is een beetje gelukt" ~ 0.5,
      goal_check_daily_string == "Ik heb mijn doel gehaald" ~ 1,
      goal_check_daily_string == "Vandaag is het niet gelukt" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

Experiment<-tb[tb$phase_FSE=="B",]
# did not remove the values after the insight conversation, because these were also not removed for the PDT analyses

# create goal variable
goal<-Experiment %>%
  group_by(Studienummer) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_goal = mean(goal_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_goal = median(goal_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_goal      = sum(!is.na(goal_numeric))  
  )

# create a compliance var (only important for the period until the evaluation converstaion)
Exp<-Experiment[Experiment$sent_date<=Experiment$T3_Evaluatiegesprek_date,]
comp<-Exp %>%
  group_by(Studienummer) %>%
  summarise(
    tb_compliance = mean(!is.na(start))
  )

# merge all data
goal<-merge(goal, comp, by="Studienummer")
df<-merge(goal, pdt, by="Studienummer")

```

# linear model FSE
```{r}
# first approach ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
fse1<-lm(effect_FSE ~ mean_goal,  data=df)
summary(fse1)

plot(df$effect_FSE, df$mean_goal)

fse2<-lm(effect_FSE ~ mean_goal + tb_compliance,  data=df)
summary(fse2)

plot(df$effect_FSE, df$mean_goal)

# linearity
plot(fse2, which = 1)
#normality of resid (QQ)
plot(fse2, which = 2)
# heterosced
plot(fse2, which = 3)

# clear outlier B10
df_no10<-df[!df$Studienummer=="B10",]

# exclude B10 -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
fse1.1<-lm(effect_FSE ~ mean_goal,  data=df_no10)
summary(fse1.1)

plot(df_no10$effect_FSE, df_no10$mean_goal)

fse2.2<-lm(effect_FSE ~ mean_goal + tb_compliance,  data=df_no10)
summary(fse2.2)

# linearity
plot(fse2.2, which = 1)
#normality of resid (QQ)
plot(fse2.2, which = 2)
# heterosced
plot(fse2.2, which = 3)

# include baseline  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
fse2.3<-lm(effect_FSE ~ mean_goal + mean_A_FSE,  data=df)
summary(fse2.3)

# linearity
plot(fse2.3, which = 1)
#normality of resid (QQ)
plot(fse2.3, which = 2)
# heterosced
plot(fse2.3, which = 3)

```

# sp correlation
```{r}
# Run tests
fse  <- cor.test(df$mean_goal, df$effect_FSE, method = "spearman")
health <- cor.test(df$mean_goal, df$effect_Health, method = "spearman")
sat <- cor.test(df$mean_goal, df$effect_Satisfaction, method = "spearman")

# Create table
results_sp <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("effect_FSE", "effect_Health", "effect_Satisfaction"),
  Spearman_rho = c(fse$estimate, health$estimate, sat$estimate),
  p_value = c(fse$p.value, health$p.value, sat$p.value)
)

```

using the Mann–Whitney U test / Fisher’s Exact Test

sex... not easy to act upon

# Load (BL) data
```{r}
# table 1 info to be loaded
bl <- read_excel(paste0(OutDir, "2026-03-23_Table1.xlsx"), sheet = "Participant_info")

# FSE responders 
bl<- bl %>% mutate(
  responder = if_else(
    Participant %in% c("B04", "B07", "B10", "B15", "B16"), 1,0
  )
)

```
# run analyses
```{r}
library(rstatix) # wilcox
wilcox_test(Fatigue_duration ~ responder, data = bl)
wilcox_test(Schoolabsence ~ responder, data = bl)
wilcox.test(Age ~ responder, data = bl)

bl %>%
  wilcox_test(Age ~ responder, exact = FALSE, ) %>%
  add_significance()


vars <- c("fatigue", "Fatigue_duration", 
          "Schoolabsence", "FSE", "Age")


mw_results <- lapply(vars, function(v) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ responder"))
  
  test <- wilcox.test(formula, data = bl)
  eff  <- wilcox_effsize(bl, formula = formula)
  
  data.frame(
    variable = v,
    W = test$statistic,
    p = test$p.value,
    effect_size = eff$effsize
  )
})

mw_results <- do.call(rbind, mw_results)

```

```{r}
vars <- c("fatigue", "Fatigue_duration", "Schoolabsence", "FSE", "Age")
bl$responder<-as.factor(bl$responder)

mw_results <- lapply(vars, function(v) {
  
  # Check if both groups exist
  sub_df <- bl %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]))
  
  if(length(unique(sub_df$responder)) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(
      variable = v,
      note = "Only one group present"
    ))
  }
  
  formula <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ responder"))
  
  # Test
  test <- wilcox.test(formula, data = sub_df, exact = FALSE)
  
  # Effect size + CI
  eff <- wilcox_effsize(sub_df, formula = formula)
  
  # Descriptives
  desc <- sub_df %>%
    group_by(responder) %>%
    summarise(
      median = median(.data[[v]], na.rm = TRUE),
      q1 = quantile(.data[[v]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q3 = quantile(.data[[v]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      min = min(.data[[v]], na.rm = TRUE),
      max = max(.data[[v]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # Ensure both groups exist
  if(nrow(desc) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(
      variable = v,
      note = "Only one group after filtering"
    ))
  }
  
  desc0 <- desc[desc$responder == 0, ]
  desc1 <- desc[desc$responder == 1, ]
  
  data.frame(
    variable = v,
    
    W = as.numeric(test$statistic),
    p = test$p.value,
    
    effect_size = eff$effsize,
    median_0 = desc0$median,
    IQR_0 = paste0(round(desc0$q1,2), "–", round(desc0$q3,2)),
    range_0 = paste0(desc0$min, "–", desc0$max),
    
    median_1 = desc1$median,
    IQR_1 = paste0(round(desc1$q1,2), "–", round(desc1$q3,2)),
    range_1 = paste0(desc1$min, "–", desc1$max)
  )
})

mw_results <- bind_rows(mw_results)

mw_results$effect_size<-round(mw_results$effect_size, 2)
mw_results$p<-signif(mw_results$p, 2)

```

# test categorial vars 
```{r}
cat_vars <- c("Education_type", "Sex")

fisher_results <- lapply(cat_vars, function(v) {
  tab <- table(bl$responder, bl[[v]])
  test <- fisher.test(tab)
  
  data.frame(
    variable = v,
    p = test$p.value
  )
})

fisher_results <- do.call(rbind, fisher_results)
```

# correlation 
```{r}

all<-merge(df, bl, by.y = "Participant", by.x = "Studienummer")

cor_results <- lapply(vars, function(v) {
  test <- cor.test(all$effect_FSE, all[[v]], method = "spearman")
  
  data.frame(
    variable = v,
    rho = test$estimate,
    p = test$p.value
  )
})

cor_results <- do.call(rbind, cor_results)
```


# save output Rq4
```{r}
library(broom)


models <- list(
  fse = fse2.3,
  health = health2,
  satis = satis2
)

results_df <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(models), function(name) {
    tidy(models[[name]]) %>%
      mutate(model = name)
  })
)


# Create a new workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "compliance_lm")
writeData(wb, sheet = "compliance_lm", results_df)


addWorksheet(wb, "compliance_sp")
writeData(wb, sheet = "compliance_sp", results_sp)

addWorksheet(wb, "respondents")
writeData(wb, sheet = "respondents", mw_results)


# Save the workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, file = paste0(OutDir, "2026-04-08_RQ4.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
```
